docs.title: Home
docs.text:
NeuBird Terminal

The Production Ops Agent in your terminal.

NeuBird connects to your telemetry databases and investigates incidents, health, cost, and performance — using natural language.

docs.title: What NeuBird Does
docs.text:
NeuBird is a terminal-native AI agent for site reliability engineering. It connects to your existing telemetry tools — PagerDuty, Datadog, CloudWatch, Grafana, GitHub, Snowflake, and 30+ more — and lets you ask questions in plain English:

  • "What services have the highest error rates right now?"
  • "Why did latency spike on api-gateway at 2am?"
  • "How much did cloud costs increase this week and what drove it?"

NeuBird queries your telemetry, reasons over results across multiple data sources, and delivers a root cause analysis — complete with evidence, sources, and recommended actions.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
Predictive analysis — Ask what's likely to page you next. NeuBird identifies degradation trends, capacity cliffs, and silent failures before they become incidents.

Pre-deployment risk assessment — Evaluate code changes before they reach production. NeuBird cross-references PRs with live telemetry to tell you what could break and why.

Agentic investigations — NeuBird doesn't just answer questions. It explores your schema, runs multiple queries, correlates data across sources, and iterates until it finds the answer. You watch the investigation unfold in real time.

Health sweeps — Run /health for a full infrastructure health check. NeuBird scans incidents, alarms, error logs, and recent deployments, then produces a Good/Bad/Ugly summary with recommended actions.

Cost analysis — /cost analyzes cloud spending trends and projects 24-hour costs with breakdowns by service, team, and resource type.

Three agent personas — Switch between investigation styles to match the situation:

Persona Model Best for Responder Claude Haiku Fast triage, immediate next actions Analyst Claude Sonnet Root cause analysis, deep investigation Architect Claude Opus Runbooks, design reviews, systemic fixes

Collapsible tool output — Press Ctrl+O to review every tool call and result from an investigation — even while it's still running. Expand individual calls to inspect full data tables, or collapse them to focus on the analysis. Works mid-investigation: pause to browse results, then press Esc to resume watching.

Local CLI integration — NeuBird automatically detects SRE tools on your machine (kubectl, docker, aws, gcloud, helm, git, terraform, curl, dig, openssl) and makes them available to the AI agent as read-only tools. Ask "how many pods are in the production namespace?" and NeuBird will run kubectl get pods directly. All commands are safety-gated — destructive operations (apply, delete, create, scale) are blocked at the code level.

Web search — When an investigation requires context beyond your telemetry — CVE details, vendor status pages, documentation, or recent outage reports — NeuBird can search the web for supporting evidence. Web search is opt-in (set ENABLE_WEBSEARCH=true) and integrates naturally into investigations alongside SQL queries and local CLI tools.

Tool inventory — On startup, NeuBird displays every tool available to the agent — grouped by source (built-in, cloud MCP, local CLI). Run /tools anytime to see the full inventory with capabilities. Example:

🔧 Tool inventory (18 tools)
  📦 Built-in (12)
     ✓ exec_sql                  Execute SQL queries against the database
     ...
  ☁️  ACE MCP (4)
     ✓ external_tool             External service queries
     ...
  💻 Local CLI (2)
     ✓ kubectl                   Read-only Kubernetes inspection (pods, logs, events)
     ✓ run_local_command         Execute read-only local CLI commands
  🔍 Detected CLIs: kubectl (v1.28.2), docker (24.0.7), git (2.39.0)
  ⬚  Not found: aws, gcloud, helm, terraform

Persistent learning — NeuBird remembers which queries work with your data sources and which telemetry tables matter for each type of investigation. It gets faster and more accurate over time.

Custom slash commands — Drop a .md file into the skills/ directory to create custom investigation templates. The filename becomes the command, and the content becomes the prompt.

Export and share — Use /export to save any investigation as a file or copy it to your clipboard. An interactive picker lets you choose format (plain text, markdown, or PDF) and scope (last answer or full conversation). Or go direct: /export pdf, /export full md, /export clipboard. PDF exports include the NeuBird logo, formatted tables, and proper section headings. Use /copy as a shortcut to copy the last answer to your clipboard instantly.

Branded PDF reports — RCA investigations, health sweeps, and cost analyses automatically generate branded PDF reports saved to ~/.config/neubird/reports/. Each report includes the NeuBird logo, data sources, investigation timeline, and structured findings with evidence tables and action items.

Live investigation dashboard — While an investigation runs, three progress bars update in real time:

  ██████████████████████████████████░░░░░░ 85% wrapping up · turn 15 · 22 tools • 52.3s
  ████████████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 50% confidence
  ████████████████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 2.4 MB · 1,247 rows · 8 queries      (Ctrl+C)

The first bar tracks investigation progress. The second shows the AI's self-reported confidence (can go down — that's useful signal). The third shows cumulative telemetry data read from SQL queries on a logarithmic scale. On completion, a summary line shows the final stats:

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ✅ completed in 3m52.1s · 17 turns · 21 tools · 80% confidence · 49.4 KB read
  📊 Data sources: config_aws_prod.aws_elbv2_target_groups, metric_aws_prod.rds_cpu

Live investigation narrative — While the agent explores schemas and runs queries, a background summarizer produces a rolling "what we know so far" status that updates after each tool round. Instead of watching raw tool calls scroll by, you see a plain-English narrative of findings and direction:

  ╭─ Investigation status ─────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
  │ Error rates on payment-service have risen from 0.1% to 3.2% in the   │
  │ last 30 minutes, concentrated on the /checkout endpoint. A deploy     │
  │ went out 45 minutes ago touching the payment retry logic. Looking     │
  │ at upstream dependencies next to rule out cascading failures.         │
  │                                                      confidence: 65%  │
  ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

The narrative is generated by a lightweight Haiku call running in parallel — it reads a snapshot of the investigation history but never modifies what Claude sees. The main investigation is not slowed or altered. The summary replaces itself on each update (not appending), so it stays compact. Web clients receive the narrative as interim_summary SSE events for rendering in a dedicated panel.

Built-in investigation skills — NeuBird ships with ready-to-use playbooks for the most common SRE workflows:

Command What it does /handoff On-call shift briefing — active incidents, recent deploys, current health, watch items /changes Compare two time windows — find every deploy, config change, metric shift, and correlate them /timeline Reconstruct a minute-by-minute incident timeline from all telemetry sources /pir Generate a leadership-ready post-incident review with 5-whys and action items /slo Calculate error budgets, burn rates, and project when SLOs will breach /blast-radius Map upstream/downstream dependencies and quantify failure impact /certs Scan TLS certificates across endpoints, flag anything expiring within 30 days

Enable them by copying to your skills directory:

cp skills/*.md ~/.config/neubird/skills/

NeuBird advertises available skills on the welcome screen so you always know what's possible — no memorization required.

Sentinel mode — Run /sentinel to activate continuous background monitoring. NeuBird's sentinel polls for new alerts every 5 minutes and runs full health sweeps every hour. It surfaces actionable findings as they appear — not on a dumb timer, but by detecting real changes in your telemetry:

> /sentinel
  🛡️ Sentinel active — polling every 5m0s, full sweep every 1h0m0s.
  Type /sentinel status to see findings, /sentinel off to stop.

  🛡️ Sentinel: 2 new finding(s) detected — type /sentinel status to review

> /sentinel status
  🛡️ Sentinel Status
  Running  · Polls every 5m0s · Sweeps every 1h0m0s
  Last poll: 14:35:12 · Last sweep: 14:30:00
  Active findings: 3

  🔴 payment-service error rate spike ✨
     Error rate jumped from 0.1% to 3.2% in the last 15 minutes
     → Investigate payment-service error rate spike and correlate with recent deploys

  🟡 auth-service connection pool at 82% ✨
     Connection pool utilization trending toward saturation
     → Check auth-service connection pool usage and project when it hits the limit

  🔵 Upcoming cert expiry: api.example.com
     TLS certificate expires in 12 days
     → Scan TLS certificates and identify renewal schedule

Use /sentinel off to stop. The sentinel runs in the background — you can investigate other things while it monitors.

MCP tool support — Extend NeuBird with Model Context Protocol servers for additional data sources and capabilities beyond SQL.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
Download the Windows .zip from the latest release, extract it, and add the folder to your PATH:

# PowerShell — download and extract
$tag = (Invoke-RestMethod "https://api.github.com/repos/neubirdai/neubird-terminal/releases/latest").tag_name
$version = $tag.TrimStart("v")
# amd64 on standard PCs, arm64 on Snapdragon / Copilot+ PCs (native and 32-bit shells report ARM64 machines correctly; an x64-emulated shell gets amd64, which still runs)
$arch = if ($env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE -eq "ARM64" -or $env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432 -eq "ARM64") { "arm64" } else { "amd64" }
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://github.com/neubirdai/neubird-terminal/releases/download/$tag/neubird_${version}_windows_${arch}.zip" -OutFile neubird.zip
Expand-Archive neubird.zip -DestinationPath "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\neubird"

# Add to PATH (current session)
$env:PATH += ";$env:LOCALAPPDATA\neubird"

# Add to PATH (permanent — requires restart)
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("PATH", $env:PATH + ";$env:LOCALAPPDATA\neubird", "User")

docs.title: Supported Data Sources
docs.text:
NeuBird connects to your existing telemetry and operations tools via read-only API integrations. Out of the box, it works with:

Incident Management — PagerDuty, Opsgenie, ServiceNow

Monitoring & Observability — Datadog, Grafana (Loki, Tempo, Mimir), CloudWatch, New Relic, Prometheus

Cloud Infrastructure — AWS (EC2, RDS, ECS, Lambda, Cost Explorer), GCP, Azure

CI/CD & Source Control — GitHub, GitLab, ArgoCD

Data Warehouses — Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift

And more — Jira, Confluence, Slack, Kubernetes, custom FDW plugins

Local CLI tools (auto-detected on your machine) — kubectl, helm, docker/podman, AWS CLI, gcloud, Azure CLI, git, terraform, curl, dig, openssl

docs.title: Server API
docs.text:
When running in server mode (neubird --server, or neubird --with-server alongside the TUI), NeuBird Terminal exposes a REST API for programmatic access:

Method Endpoint Description GET /health Server health check GET /metrics Prometheus metrics POST /v1/infer Run an investigation (SSE streaming) POST /v1/infer/cancel Cancel a running investigation GET /v1/infer/status Status of running investigations GET /v1/infer/stream Re-attach to a running investigation's stream GET /v1/tools?session_id=... List available tools for a session GET /v1/skills List available investigation skills POST /v1/sentinel/start Start sentinel mode POST /v1/sentinel/stop Stop sentinel mode GET /v1/sentinel/status Sentinel status and config GET /v1/sentinel/findings Current sentinel findings POST /v1/sessions/reset Reset conversation history POST /v1/sessions/delete Delete a session POST /v1/sessions/feedback Submit rating or insight POST /v1/prompt/submit Submit a prompt for async processing (returns prompt_id)

All routes except /health sit behind X-Desktop-Secret auth when a desktop secret is configured (the server is open when run by hand with no secret). For the engine internals — agent loop, tool system, context management, personas — see docs/architecture.md; for how NeuBird learns and remembers, see docs/MEMORY_SYSTEM.md.

docs.title: Async Prompt Queue
docs.text:
Prompts can be submitted to a Redis-backed queue instead of the synchronous /v1/infer endpoint. Any agent pod with access to the same Redis picks up the prompt and processes it. This enables horizontal scaling — add more pods to process more prompts in parallel.

# Submit a prompt
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/prompt/submit \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "Why did latency spike on api-gateway?", "project_uuid": "your-project-id"}'

# Response: {"prompt_id": "a1b2c3d4-..."}

The request body accepts the same fields as /v1/infer. If prompt_id is omitted, one is generated automatically.

Reading results — The agent streams output to Redis at <org>:response:<prompt_id>. (A synchronous /v1/infer called with "stream_to_redis": true writes the same key, holding the UI stream as raven relays it — see docs/api/infer-endpoint.md.) Poll the status key <org>:response:<prompt_id>:status for the current state:

Status Meaning processing An agent is actively working on the prompt complete Prompt finished successfully dead_letter Prompt failed after exhausting all retries

Retries and dead-letter — If an agent crashes or fails mid-prompt, the message stays in the queue and is automatically reclaimed by another agent after a configurable idle period. After the maximum number of delivery attempts (default 3), the prompt is moved to a dead-letter stream (<org>:prompt:deadletter) and marked dead_letter so it is not retried forever.

Configuration:

Env var Description Default REDIS_URI Redis connection string redis://127.0.0.1:6379 ORG_NAME Org prefix for all Redis keys local PROMPT_QUEUE_MAX_CONCURRENT Max parallel prompt workers per pod 8 PROMPT_QUEUE_AUTOCLAIM_IDLE Idle time before a stalled prompt is reclaimed 25m PROMPT_QUEUE_MAX_RETRIES Max delivery attempts before dead-letter 3 PROMPT_QUEUE_RETENTION How long processed queue and dead-letter entries are kept; trimmed on every enqueue and hourly 168h PROMPT_QUEUE_TRIM_INTERVAL How often the consumer trims history and prunes idle consumers 1h PROMPT_QUEUE_CONSUMER_TTL Idle time before a consumer with nothing pending is removed from the group 168h

The consumer loop starts automatically when Redis is reachable. If Redis is not configured, the /v1/prompt/submit endpoint is not registered and only synchronous /v1/infer is available.

docs.title: Sentinel API
docs.text:
Start sentinel monitoring via the API:

# Start sentinel with custom intervals
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/sentinel/start \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"poll_interval": "5m", "sweep_interval": "30m", "project_uuid": "your-project-id"}'

# Check findings
curl http://localhost:8080/v1/sentinel/findings

# Stop sentinel
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/sentinel/stop

All endpoints require the X-Desktop-Secret header when DESKTOP_SECRET is set.

docs.title: SSE Event Types
docs.text:
The /v1/infer endpoint streams Server-Sent Events. Each event is a JSON object with a type field:

SSE Event Type Go Callback TUI Handler Web Proxy (falcon.py) Description chunk OnText sp.AddText() Code-fence filter → RCA suppressor → yield markdown Streamed text from Claude (investigation narration, final answer, Opus synthesis) tool_start OnToolExec (IsStart=true) sp.AddToolStart() update_status with friendly label, CoT tracker Agent begins executing a tool tool_done OnToolExec (IsStart=false) sp.AddToolResult() Renders markdown table or hides exploratory errors Tool execution completed (output may be truncated to 8KB) tool_data OnToolData sp.AddToolData() Fallback table render from full JSON; stores raw SQL results Full structured output from data-producing tools (not truncated) data_read OnDataRead sp.SetDataRead() Logs bytes/rows/queries, updates CoT tracker Cumulative telemetry data volume (bytes, rows, queries from exec_sql) progress OnProgress sp.SetProgress() update_progress(pct, confidence), CoT state Investigation progress percentage, phase, and confidence phase OnPhase sp.SetAgentPhase() → overrides progress bar label Yields demarcated falcon_phase JSON block Agent phase transition: investigating, answering, synthesizing turn OnTurn sp.SetTurn() Not handled (logged, ignored) LLM iteration number within the tool-use loop trace OnTrace sp.SetTraceID() Not handled (logged, ignored) OpenTelemetry trace ID for Langfuse correlation sources OnSources sp.SetSourceSummary() Stored; emitted as CONTENT_TYPE_SOURCES in finally block Data sources (tables, URLs) used in the investigation health_report OnHealthReport RenderHealthSummaryTiles() → sp.AddText() Yields inline markdown block Sonnet's structured health findings (mid-stream, before Opus synthesis) rca_saved OnRCASaved Not wired (TUI reads file paths from text) Persists RCA markdown + structured JSON to the session store Opus synthesis report saved as PDF/markdown session_metadata OnSessionMetadata Not wired Yields demarcated JSON; persists to session store on COMPLETED Running investigation metadata (cost, timing, actions, time-saved) rating_request OnRatingRequest Not wired Logged, ignored (Raven UI handles ratings) Signal to show a thumbs-up/down prompt interim_summary OnInterimSummary sp.SetInterimSummary() Yields demarcated interim_summary JSON block Background "what we know so far" narrative (Haiku, after each tool round) synthesizing — — Updates status spinner Signal that the synthesis pass is starting summary_text OnSummaryText Not wired (falls through to OnText) Logged (same content arrives via chunk) Synthesis/answer text on a dedicated channel for clients that distinguish it error OnError sp.SetError() Yields warning message, breaks stream loop Non-recoverable error (or synthetic event from connection loss)

docs.title: Investigation Flow
docs.text:
Every investigation follows this sequence. The synthesis pass runs unless the agent disabled it or no sources were gathered (see When the Synthesis Pass Runs below).

User question
  │
  ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Phase: investigating  (Sonnet tool loop)                       │
│                                                                 │
│  Events: chunk, tool_start, tool_done, tool_data, data_read,   │
│          progress, turn, interim_summary                        │
│                                                                 │
│  Claude iterates: think → call tools → observe results → think  │
│  Tools execute in parallel. Up to 25 iterations per batch.      │
│  Each iteration is one SendMessageStream API call.              │
│                                                                 │
│  After each tool round, a background Haiku call produces a      │
│  rolling "what we know so far" narrative (interim_summary).     │
│  This is a read-only side-channel — it never modifies Claude's  │
│  context window or alters the investigation flow.               │
│                                                                 │
│  Loop exits when:                                               │
│    • StopReason = "end_turn" → Claude is done (normal exit)     │
│    • StopReason = "max_tokens" → auto-continue with same state  │
│    • StopReason = "tool_use" → execute tools, loop again        │
│    • Iteration limit (25) hit → summarize, ask to continue      │
└─────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
              │
              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Phase: answering  (Sonnet final turn)                          │
│                                                                 │
│  Events: phase("answering")                                     │
│                                                                 │
│  Sonnet's last text was already streamed during the loop.       │
│  This phase marker tells clients the investigation is complete  │
│  and any future chunks are the report.                          │
└─────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
              │
              ▼
        ┌──────────────────┐
        │ Synthesis pass?  │──── No ──── skip to completion
        └────────┬─────────┘
                 │ Yes
                 ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Phase: synthesizing                                            │
│                                                                 │
│  Events: phase("synthesizing"), health_report (health only),    │
│          chunk (report text), rca_saved                          │
│                                                                 │
│  Report pass: one more turn on the run's own model and system   │
│  prompt, reading the prefix the loop just cached. Health/cost   │
│  instead hand off to Opus for a senior review.                  │
│  Text streams as chunk events — the user reads it live.         │
│  A PDF/markdown report is saved automatically.                  │
└─────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
              │
              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Completion                                                     │
│                                                                 │
│  Events: session_metadata (COMPLETED), sources, rating_request, │
│          phase not emitted — OnDone fires                       │
│                                                                 │
│  TUI: green "✅ completed in ..." footer bar                    │
│  Server: [DONE] SSE sentinel                                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: When the Synthesis Pass Runs
docs.text:
Every investigation ends in a synthesis pass unless the agent sets disable_synthesis or the run gathered no sources at all. The question's wording no longer decides whether a pass runs — only which of the three flavors it gets.

Investigation Type Question Detection Minimum Sources Function Health Question starts with "Run a rapid infrastructure health assessment." (generated by /health slash command) ≥ 3 runHealthSynthesis — Opus senior SRE review of Good/Bad/Ugly findings Cost Question starts with the cost analysis prefix (generated by /cost slash command) ≥ 2 runCostSynthesis — Opus cost trend extrapolation and ROI-ranked cuts Report pass Everything else ≥ 1 runSynthesis — the final report, written by the run's own model No pass disable_synthesis: true, or 0 sources queried — The loop's own last message is the final output

The report pass is one extra turn appended to the investigation the loop just finished. It runs on the run's own model and its own system prompt — not on a separate Opus agent — so the request rebuilds the identical tools → system → messages prefix the loop's last turn wrote to the prompt cache. The whole investigation comes back as cached input and only the appended instruction turn is billed fresh, which is what makes it affordable to run every time.

Everything the pass needs to be told therefore rides in that appended user turn rather than in a system prompt: the output format, the citation contract, any tool-access gaps, and open claim challenges. Editing the system prompt or the tools array for the pass would drop the cache and cost more than the pass saves.

Output format is owned by skills, so it is customer-configurable end to end:

  • If the project has SKILL_TYPE_SUMMARY skills, they own the format and compose with each other.
  • Otherwise the built-in final-report skill supplies the default. Because it is an ordinary skill in skills/, a deployment can replace the whole default format by dropping a same-named skill into HAWKEYE_SKILLS_DIR.

docs.title: Stream Retry on Transient Errors
docs.text:
When the Anthropic API drops the connection mid-stream (HTTP/2 reset, INTERNAL_ERROR, TCP reset), the agent retries the current LLM call automatically. The conversation history is intact — the failed partial response was never appended — so Claude regenerates from the same state.

  • Up to 2 retries with 3s / 6s backoff
  • User sees 🔄 LLM connection lost, retrying (1/2)... inline
  • Applies to both the Sonnet investigation loop and tool-use iterations
  • Non-transient errors (auth failures, rate limits, context cancellation) are not retried

docs.title: Thin-Answer Conclusion Injection
docs.text:
Claude sometimes stops after gathering evidence without writing a conclusion — especially on lower-confidence investigations where it queried data but didn't synthesize findings. The user sees tool results followed immediately by the green completion bar with no analysis in between.

The agent detects this and injects a conclusion prompt automatically:

  • Triggers when: end_turn with < 200 characters of text AND ≥ 3 tool calls were executed
  • What happens: A conclusion prompt is appended to the conversation and one more SendMessageStream call is made without tools (so Claude writes text only — no more queries)
  • User sees: The analysis streams in naturally, as if Claude had written it in the first place
  • Safety: Only fires once per investigation (concludedOnce flag prevents loops). If the conclusion call fails, the investigation completes normally — the user still has all the evidence from the tool calls

This does not apply to simple questions (< 3 tool calls) where Claude's short answer is appropriate, nor to cases where Claude wrote a substantial response alongside its last tool call.

pip install mkdocs-material

# Serve docs locally at http://localhost:8000
make docs

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: The docs system has three layers:

docs.title: 1. Content Generation (make docs-gen)
docs.text:
Runs automatically as part of make docs. Generates:

  • docs/index.md — produced from README.md with a transform that swaps the GitHub asciinema badge for an inline interactive player
  • docs/configuration/flags.md — auto-generated from Go source code (internal/docmeta/)
  • docs/configuration/env-vars.md — auto-generated from Go source code

You never edit docs/index.md directly — edit README.md instead.

docs.title: 2. Demo Recordings (make record-demos)
docs.text:
Run manually when demo scenarios or TUI rendering code changes. Requires external tools:

# Install recording dependencies (once)
brew install asciinema charmbracelet/tap/freeze
# tmux is usually already installed

This builds the neubird binary, then for each demos/*.yaml scenario:

docs.title: Memory System — How Falcon Learns and Remembers
docs.text: This document explains how Falcon accumulates knowledge across investigations — from raw capture by agents to background assimilation into a searchable, vector-backed memory store.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Falcon uses a two-phase memory architecture to turn observations from investigations into durable, reusable knowledge:

  1. Raw capture — agents write learnings in real-time during investigations
  2. Assimilation — a background job consolidates and embeds raw learnings into a searchable store

Memories are scoped strictly to a project, persist across sessions, and are retrieved at investigation time to guide agents toward better answers.

docs.title: Short-Term vs Long-Term Memory
docs.text:
"Memory" spans two very different systems. Short-term memory is falcon's in-context conversation management (covered in depth in architecture.md → Context management); long-term memory is the ACE-backed store this document describes. The seam between them:

flowchart LR
    subgraph short ["Short-term (falcon process, per session)"]
        TURN["Current turn<br/>streamed blocks"]
        INV["Current investigation<br/>Session.Messages<br/>(offload + trim per turn)"]
        PRIOR["Earlier investigations,<br/>same session<br/>(compressOldHistory summaries)"]
    end
    subgraph bridge ["Conversation history (ACE)"]
        ACEH["saveACEHistory / LoadACEHistory<br/>injected next session at<br/>tier 1 (full blocks) or 2/3 (compressed)"]
    end
    subgraph long ["Long-term knowledge (ACE, this doc)"]
        RAW[("Raw tables<br/>sql / table / user_insights / tool")]
        ASSIM[("assimilated_learnings<br/>pgvector, per-project")]
    end

    TURN --> INV --> PRIOR
    INV -->|"end of run"| ACEH
    INV -->|"save_learnings during run"| RAW
    RAW -->|"MemoryAssimilator (6h cron)"| ASSIM
    ASSIM -->|"load_relevant_learnings +<br/>prompt sections"| INV
    ACEH -->|"next session"| INV

Conversation history answers "what did we say/do before"; the learnings store answers "what do we know" — deduplicated, embedded, and searchable independent of any conversation.

docs.title: How Memory Reaches the Model (Falcon Runtime)
docs.text: The ACE tools above are only half the story. The falcon side (internal/ai/agent.go) decides when memory is fetched, where it lands, and which agents see which parts.

docs.title: Stub override and session scoping
docs.text:
Falcon ships built-in stubs for save_learnings, load_relevant_learnings, and update_memory (tools.go). At NewAgent, these names are deliberately excluded from the duplicate-suppression map so ACE's tools/list overrides them — the wire schema and behavior are ACE's, while the stub definitions remain the offline fallback. Get-all tools (user_insights, table_learnings, sql_learnings) arrive HiddenFromLLM: registered with a session, callable by falcon code, never shown to the model.

Each prompt opens its own ACE session and closes it on release (mcp_pool.go, agent.go), scoped by connect_database({database: projectUUID}) — project identity is session state, never a tool parameter. The learning queue is the exception: it keeps its own long-lived background session per project (learning_queue.go) so its writes never compete with the prompt's.

docs.title: Investigation-time flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    EX["Execute(prompt)"] --> PRE["ensureMemoryLoaded(prompt) — once per agent<br/>load_relevant_learnings(query=prompt, include_raw=true)<br/>(skipped when cfg.DisableMemory — eval 'memory off' arm)"]
    PRE --> MERGE["mergeMemoryResult routes each entry by type<br/>(memorySeenIDs dedups across loads;<br/>deleted ids are pinned so they never re-merge)"]
    MERGE -->|sql| SQLC["sqlLearnings cache → SQL-learnings section"]
    MERGE -->|table| TBLC["table cache → Table-knowledge section"]
    MERGE -->|tool| HINT["tool hints → Tool-hints section"]
    MERGE -->|"insight (provenance)"| INS["insights cache → User-insights section<br/>explicit: always rendered<br/>inferred: only with 'inferred_insights' opt-in"]
    MERGE -->|tribal_knowledge| SKIP["no local cache — recall-on-demand only"]

    SQLC & TBLC & HINT & INS --> GATE{"AgentDefinition.ContextSections<br/>('context:' frontmatter) opt-in?"}
    GATE -->|yes| FROZEN["Sections FROZEN into statics per run<br/>(mid-run saves don't bust the prompt cache)"]
    GATE -->|no| OMIT["Section omitted for this agent"]
    FROZEN --> SYS["System prompt<br/>(+ promptsections.MemoryTools() guidance<br/>when 'learnings' is enabled)"]

    SYS --> LOOP["Agent loop"]
    LOOP -->|"model calls load_relevant_learnings"| L2["Result returned to model AND<br/>merged into caches (single MCP call)"]
    LOOP -->|"model calls save_learnings"| SV["Forwarded to ACE async (rawInput verbatim,<br/>defaults written back) + local caches updated"]
    LOOP -->|"model calls update_memory"| UM["Forwarded to ACE;<br/>on delete: id pinned in memorySeenIDs"]
    LOOP -->|"exec_sql error"| AUTO["autoSaveColumnLearning / autoSaveGroupByLearning<br/>+ MANDATORY save_learnings nudge appended<br/>to the tool result"]
    SV --> QUEUE["learning_queue.go — 2 background workers<br/>persist to ACE with explicit project_uuid"]

Legacy fallbacks: without an ACE save_learnings session, writes route to the older per-type ACE tools via EnqueueLearning, or to the local jsonl stores (internal/learnings, internal/tablelearnings, internal/feedback) — which are caches/queues, not the source of truth.

docs.title: Sharp edges (falcon side)
docs.text:
• user_insights get-all emits raw ids as raw-<N>, but update_memory routes raw insight ids as insight-<N> — callers must translate the prefix.
  • table_learnings get-all returns no ids, so its rows are currently untargetable by update_memory's table-N route.
  • Memory tools are excluded from isDataTool, so their output never counts toward data-read metrics (desktop shows DATA 0 B for memory-only runs — by design).
  • cfg.DisableMemory both strips the memory tools (deny-list) and turns off every memory-derived prompt section, fully isolating the A/B "memory off" arm.

docs.title: Memory Types
docs.text:
Type What it stores Example sql Query patterns and rules for specific tables/schemas "Always filter events by org_id first for performance" table Which tables map to which investigation scenarios "Use deployments + rollbacks for deploy-regression queries" insight User-stated knowledge and agent-derived observations "User prefers percentile breakdowns over averages for latency" tool Syntax error patterns for specific tools "Pass tables as an array of strings, not comma-separated" tribal_knowledge Environment/org facts recalled on demand only "The payments team owns the txn_* schemas; page #payments-oncall"

User insights are classified by provenance: explicit (user directly stated) or inferred (agent derived). Explicit insights are always recalled; inferred insights are recalled by semantic similarity only — and are rendered in the system prompt only for agents that opt into the inferred_insights context section.

tribal_knowledge shares the provenance field (default inferred) but is never injected into the system prompt on the falcon side: it is recalled on demand via load_relevant_learnings(type="tribal_knowledge") and has no local cache (see the runtime section below). It is not a save_learnings type: the store is written only through the dedicated save_tribal_knowledge tool, an agent-restricted builtin held solely by the Slack/Teams capture listeners; every other agent records team/operational facts as insight. The tool forwards to the ACE save_learnings session with the type injected by the dispatch handler, and has no legacy fallback — without an ACE session the save errors rather than misfiling the fact.

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text: All memory lives in the ace PostgreSQL schema, backed by the pgvector extension.

docs.title: Raw Tables (write-first, unprocessed)
docs.text:
ace.sql_learnings        — SQL rules keyed by schema_table_type
ace.table_learnings      — scenario-to-table mappings with investigation context
ace.user_insights        — user corrections, preferences, facts
ace.tool_learnings       — tool syntax error patterns keyed by tool_name

All four tables carry a project_uuid TEXT NOT NULL column (added in migration 20260521000001_learnings_project_uuid). Every raw row starts with assimilated_at IS NULL. The background job sets this field once the row has been consolidated.

Partial indexes on (project_uuid) WHERE assimilated_at IS NULL enable fast per-project discovery of pending work.

docs.title: Consolidated Store
docs.text:
ace.assimilated_learnings
Column Type Purpose id UUID Primary key project_uuid TEXT Project this memory belongs to (strict equality filter) type TEXT sql | table | user_insight | tool learning TEXT The consolidated knowledge summary TEXT 1–2 sentence executive summary embedding vector(512) Semantic vector for similarity search confidence FLOAT 0.0–1.0, set by the assimilation agent source_ids TEXT[] Back-references to raw row IDs trigger TEXT Deprecated; explicit provenance now controls always-load behavior schema_table_type TEXT Lookup key for SQL learnings investigation_type TEXT Context for table learnings insight_type TEXT Deprecated; provenance replaces subtypes provenance TEXT "explicit" (user stated) or "inferred" (agent derived) tool_name TEXT Lookup key for tool learnings deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ Soft-delete timestamp

An HNSW index on embedding and a partial index on project_uuid WHERE deleted_at IS NULL support fast retrieval.

docs.title: Project Scoping
docs.text:
All memory is strictly scoped to a single project. Every read and write operation filters by project_uuid = $N — there is no fallback to empty-UUID rows or cross-project sharing.

  • Raw tables — project_uuid stored on insert; unassimilated queries filter by it
  • Assimilated store — all search, upsert, merge, and delete operations include WHERE project_uuid = $N
  • save_learnings tool — reads project_uuid from MCP args or the current session
  • list_unassimilated_learnings — filters by project_uuid when provided, so the MemoryAssimilator pre-hook only fires for projects that actually have pending work

This was tightened in #276, which removed the backward-compatibility IN ($projectUUID, '') fallback and added project_uuid to all three raw tables.

docs.title: ACE Tools (MCP)
docs.text: All memory operations are exposed as MCP tools, implemented in ace/tools/.

docs.title: save_learnings
docs.text:
Writes a raw learning to the appropriate raw table.

save_learnings(type, content, ...)
  → writes to sql_learnings, table_learnings, user_insights, or tool_learnings
  → stores project_uuid from MCP args or session context
  → assimilated_at = NULL (pending)
  → returns {"status": "ok", "type": "<type>"}

Called by agents during or after investigations. Non-blocking.

Source: ace/tools/save_memory/mcp_tool_save_memory.go

docs.title: load_relevant_learnings
docs.text:
Retrieves ranked learnings from assimilated_learnings using hybrid search, scoped to project_uuid.

load_relevant_learnings(query, type?, min_score?, include_raw?)
  → hybrid: vector similarity (HNSW) + text search (ts_rank) via RRF
  → fallback: keyword-only if embedding unavailable
  → returns {learnings: [...]} where each entry has score, confidence, similarity, source

Search strategy per type:

  • SQL — exact match on schema_table_type (no vector needed)
  • Table — Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) of vector + text, blended with confidence: 0.75 × RRF + 0.25 × confidence
  • User insights — vector similarity + always-trigger records appended
  • Tool — exact match on tool_name, or semantic query when tool_name is omitted

Pass include_raw=true during assimilation to also see raw rows that haven't been written yet, enabling deduplication within the current batch.

Returns up to 10 learnings per type, filtered at min relevance 0.35.

Source: ace/tools/load_relevant/mcp_tool_load_relevant.go

docs.title: update_memory
docs.text:
Deletes or modifies an existing memory. Called when a user corrects an agent.

update_memory(id, action)
  → id: UUID (assimilated) or "insight-N" (raw insight)
  → action: "delete" (soft) or "modify" (content update)

Cascade behavior for raw deletes:

  • Soft-deletes the raw row
  • Finds all assimilated records containing the raw ID in source_ids
  • Single-source assimilated record → auto soft-deleted
  • Multi-source assimilated record → returned as assimilated_needs_review for agent to edit

Source: ace/tools/update_memory/mcp_tool_update_memory.go

docs.title: list_unassimilated_learnings
docs.text:
Discovery tool for the MemoryAssimilator agent. Returns up to 50 rows per type from the last 10 days where assimilated_at IS NULL, filtered by project_uuid. Covers all four raw tables in a single call:

{
  "sql_learnings":   [...],
  "table_learnings": [...],
  "user_insights":   [...],
  "tool_learnings":  [...]
}

Restricted: agent-only (not exposed to user-facing agents).

Source: ace/tools/list_unassimilated_learnings/mcp_tool_list_unassimilated.go

docs.title: describe_table
docs.text: Returns schema information for a table. Now also injects SQL hints from assimilated_learnings into its response (Hints []string field), surfacing relevant memory directly at query-planning time without a separate load_relevant_learnings call.

docs.title: update_learning_assimilation
docs.text:
Writes an assimilation result: creates or merges into assimilated_learnings, then marks the raw row as processed.

update_learning_assimilation(table, id, learning, summary, confidence, ...)
  → inserts new assimilated record OR merges into existing (append source_id)
  → sets assimilated_at = now() on the raw row
  → generates 512-dim embedding for table/insight types

Restricted: MemoryAssimilator agent only.

Source: ace/tools/update_learning_assimilation/mcp_tool_update_assimilation.go

docs.title: MemoryAssimilator
docs.text:
Location: agents/MemoryAssimilator.md

A background-only agent (not user-invocable) that consolidates raw learnings into the assimilated store.

Property Value Model claude-haiku-4-5 (cost-capped at $8/run) Timeout 15 minutes Schedule Every 6 hours per project (cron: 0 */6 * * *) User invocable No Session footprint None (skip_save_session: true)

Tools available: list_unassimilated_learnings, update_learning_assimilation, load_relevant_learnings, update_memory, get_skill, get_prompt

Skills loaded per type: memory-sql-learnings, memory-table-learnings, memory-user-insights, memory-forget-requests, memory-tool-learnings

Pre-execution hook: Before the agent runs, CheckNeedsLearning calls list_unassimilated_learnings scoped to the project. If no pending rows exist the run is skipped entirely, avoiding unnecessary Haiku calls.

docs.title: ExecLearningsAgent
docs.text:
Location: agents/ExecLearningsAgent.md

The user-facing agent behind the Falcon Learnings tab (and the desktop Memory page). It is the memory agent for engineering / IT managers: it reads and writes Falcon's memory and answers at management altitude — what keeps recurring, what was investigated but never resolved, what the team knows and where that knowledge has holes.

Memory-only, deliberately. A revision on this branch granted the delivery integrations (Jira, GitHub, Confluence, ServiceNow) via read-verb globs so the agent could cross memory against live delivery data. Testing on the copeyemg tenant showed that grant is not a real boundary and the integrations were pulled back out. See "Why no integrations" below before re-adding them.

Property Value Model claude-opus-5-5 User invocable Yes (Falcon Learnings tab / desktop Memory page) Tools (exclusive — no *) load_relevant_learnings, search_prompts, save_learnings, update_memory, list_charts, emit_table, code_exec, get_skill Skills The SOUL is self-contained; get_skill is retained for skills explicitly offered to the agent External access None. No integrations, no tool_search, no exec_sql. Memory is the only source. Context sections insights Base prompt agents/ExecLearningsAgent/SOUL.md (full base — Analyst.md not loaded)

Confidence is fed asynchronously by the interim summarizer (no model-facing confidence tool exists). Runs that never get a summarizer call — sub-10s answers, DisableInterimSummary agents — show the completion floor (75) in the UI, and their Langfuse final_confidence metadata is omitted rather than fabricated.

Memory workflow:

  1. Calls load_relevant_learnings for each type at the start of an investigation
  2. Searches past investigation history via search_prompts
  3. Detects gaps: investigations with no save_learnings call = unresolved knowledge
  4. Saves new learnings inline via save_learnings
  5. On user correction: load_relevant_learnings → update_memory (delete) → save_learnings (new)
  6. Crosses the two memory sources against each other — topics investigated repeatedly with no save_learnings call are the unresolved gaps, and are the agent's headline finding
  7. Emits a ready-to-paste ticket draft for anything unresolved — it cannot file anything, and is told never to claim, promise, or offer otherwise

Why no integrations (read before re-adding them):

A revision on this branch granted Jira/GitHub/Confluence/ServiceNow reads through read-verb globs — atlassian__get*, github*__list*, servicenow*__list* — chosen so no pattern could match a write tool. Verified against 99 real tool names from the copeyemg tenant, the matcher denied every write. It still wasn't a boundary:

  • def.Tools gates visibility, not execution. The allowlist is applied when building the per-turn tool list (agent.go ~7958). executeTool (~12207) dispatches anything present in the MCP registry and never consults rs.allowedTools.
  • tool_search advertises the whole deferred catalog. buildToolSearchDescription (tool_search.go:495) filters only AgentRestricted, not the run's allowlist — so tools outside the grant are offered to the model with their schemas.
  • The write tools were not AgentRestricted on that tenant. They appeared in tool_search output, which skips restricted tools. So nothing downstream filtered them.

Observed: pagerduty__get_incident and github__list_pull_requests both executed while matching no pattern in the grant.

Granting integrations safely needs a dispatch-time allowlist check in internal/ai, not a longer glob list. Until that exists, TestExecLearnings_{NoWildcard,NoToolSearch,NoIntegrationTools} hold the line.

docs.title: Assimilation: Per-Type Logic
docs.text:
The MemoryAssimilator orchestrates five steps (defined in agents/MemoryAssimilator/SOUL.md):

  1. Call list_unassimilated_learnings to discover all pending rows for the project
  2. Call get_skill() for each type present to load its assimilation rules
  3. Process each batch using the loaded skills
  4. Handle any [FORGET] rows via the memory-forget-requests skill
  5. Report total rows assimilated and forget requests processed

Critical rule across all types: always pass include_raw=true when calling load_relevant_learnings during assimilation, so raw rows from the current batch are visible for deduplication before they are written.

docs.title: SQL Learnings (memory-sql-learnings)
docs.text:
Skill: skills/memory-sql-learnings/SKILL.md

SQL learnings are upserted — one active assimilated record exists per schema_table_type. Subsequent raw rows update that record rather than creating duplicates.

For each raw sql_learnings row:

  1. Call update_learning_assimilation with:
  2. table="sql_learnings", the row ID, generalized learning, summary, confidence, schema_table_type
  3. This upserts by schema_table_type, updating the existing record if one exists

SQL hints are served directly via describe_table, which queries assimilated_learnings and injects relevant hints into its response. There is no separate table-comment update step.

Confidence bands:

Range Meaning > 0.8 Generic rules applicable across many environments 0.5 – 0.8 Patterns applicable to recognizable situations < 0.5 Narrow, investigation-specific facts

docs.title: Table Learnings (memory-table-learnings)
docs.text:
Skill: skills/memory-table-learnings/SKILL.md

Table learnings accumulate over time and are merged when a new row is semantically identical or very similar to an existing one.

For each raw table_learnings row:

  1. Validate against investigation context (if prompt_id present):
  2. Call get_prompt() to retrieve the investigation
  3. Cross-reference tool calls and final_answer to validate which candidate tables actually had evidence
  4. Update the tables field to only include validated tables
  5. If get_prompt fails → treat as no context, proceed with confidence 0.5

  6. If investigation status is not COMPLETED or confidence < 0.5 → mark inconclusive (confidence 0.1)

  7. Deduplicate via load_relevant_learnings(type="table", include_raw=true):

  8. Identical → merge with merge_into_id=<existing_id> (no new record)
  9. Same insight, slight variation → merge with updated learning capturing both cases; increase confidence by ≤ 0.1
  10. Multiple near-duplicates → delete all but the highest-confidence record, merge into the survivor

  11. Different insight → proceed to step 3

  12. Insert as new via update_learning_assimilation with table_learnings data

docs.title: User Insights (memory-user-insights)
docs.text:
Skill: skills/memory-user-insights/SKILL.md

User insights are merged or inserted based on semantic similarity. The trigger field controls whether a preference is always returned or only returned on semantic match.

For each raw user_insights row (excluding [FORGET] rows):

  1. Deduplicate via load_relevant_learnings(type="insight", include_raw=true):
  2. Identical → merge with merge_into_id=<existing_id> (no new record)
  3. Same belief, updated → call update_memory(action="modify") on the existing record, then merge the raw row via merge_into_id
  4. Multiple near-duplicates → delete all but highest-confidence survivor, then modify + merge into it

  5. Different insight → proceed to step 2

  6. Insert as new via update_learning_assimilation. Provenance is carried forward from the raw row automatically — explicit insights are always recalled, inferred insights by semantic similarity only.

docs.title: Forget Requests (memory-forget-requests)
docs.text:
Skill: skills/memory-forget-requests/SKILL.md

Any user_insights row whose content starts with [FORGET] is treated as an erasure request rather than a new learning.

For each [FORGET] row:

  1. Extract the subject from the content after the [FORGET] prefix
  2. Call load_relevant_learnings(type="insight", query=<subject>) to find matching records
  3. For each match, call update_memory(action="delete", id=<id>) to soft-delete it
  4. If no match found, no action needed — the raw row was never assimilated

docs.title: Tool Learnings (memory-tool-learnings)
docs.text:
Skill: skills/memory-tool-learnings/SKILL.md

Tool learnings are upserted — one active assimilated record exists per tool_name. Subsequent raw rows update that record rather than creating duplicates.

For each batch of raw tool_learnings rows:

  1. Group by tool_name
  2. Compile a concise hint block noting bad patterns, correct forms, and frequency
  3. Call update_learning_assimilation with table="tool_learnings", row ID, compiled learning, summary, confidence, tool_name

docs.title: Full Data Flow
docs.text:
Investigation (ExecLearningsAgent / Analyst)
  │
  ├── load_relevant_learnings(query, project_uuid)
  │     └── hybrid search on assimilated_learnings WHERE project_uuid = ?
  │           → returns ranked context for agent
  │
  ├── agent reasons, executes SQL, presents findings
  │
  └── save_learnings(type, content, project_uuid, ...)
        └── writes to raw table with project_uuid (assimilated_at = NULL)

                         ↓  (every 6 hours, per project)

Memory Assimilation (MemoryAssimilator)
  │
  ├── [pre-hook] CheckNeedsLearning(project_uuid)
  │     └── aborts if no pending rows for this project
  │
  ├── list_unassimilated_learnings(project_uuid)
  │     └── up to 50 rows per type, last 10 days
  │
  ├── get_skill for each type present
  │
  ├── SQL learnings:
  │     └── upsert by schema_table_type into assimilated_learnings
  │
  ├── Table learnings:
  │     ├── validate against investigation context (get_prompt)
  │     ├── deduplicate via load_relevant_learnings (include_raw=true)
  │     └── insert new or merge into existing
  │
  ├── User insights:
  │     ├── deduplicate via load_relevant_learnings (include_raw=true)
  │     ├── set trigger="always" for preferences only
  │     └── insert new or merge/modify existing
  │
  ├── Tool learnings:
  │     └── upsert by tool_name into assimilated_learnings
  │
  └── [FORGET] rows:
        ├── find matching assimilated records
        └── soft-delete each match

                         ↓

Next investigation:
  ├── describe_table(table) → hints from assimilated_learnings injected into response
  ├── tool descriptions loaded → hints from assimilated_learnings appended to description
  └── load_relevant_learnings(type="tool") → tool hints injected into ## Tool usage rules section

docs.title: Learning Queue
docs.text:
Location: internal/ai/learning_queue.go

A background worker pool (2 goroutines) that persists learnings from Falcon agents to ACE asynchronously. Each job carries a project_uuid because background sessions are not connected to a database session.

docs.title: Key Design Decisions
docs.text:
Strict project isolation — All queries use project_uuid = $N with no cross-project fallback. Removed in #276 was the IN ($projectUUID, '') pattern that had allowed org-wide system records.

Soft deletes everywhere — deleted_at timestamps preserve audit history and allow undo. Queries always filter WHERE deleted_at IS NULL.

Two-phase architecture — Raw capture is non-blocking; expensive operations (embedding generation, deduplication, merging) happen asynchronously in the background job.

Assimilation idempotence — SQL learnings upsert by schema_table_type (one record per table). assimilated_at prevents the same raw row from being processed twice.

Hybrid search with graceful degradation — Vector + text search combined via RRF for table and user insight types. Falls back to keyword-only search if the embedder is unavailable.

Multi-source merge tracking — source_ids TEXT[] links each assimilated record back to its raw sources, enabling safe cascade deletes and transparent lineage.

Always-trigger preferences — User insights of subtype preference are tagged trigger="always" so they are returned on every load_relevant_learnings call, regardless of semantic similarity. Other subtypes are returned only when the query matches.

docs.title: SSO Login Implementation
docs.text: This document describes the SSO (Single Sign-On) login feature added to NeuBird Falcon CLI.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Falcon now supports OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) for secure browser-based authentication. This allows users to log in using their organization's SSO provider (Okta, Azure AD, Google, etc.) instead of entering username/password directly in the CLI.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
1. OAuth Client (internal/oauth/client.go)
  2. Implements OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE
  3. Generates cryptographically secure code verifier and challenge
  4. Starts local HTTP callback server on ports 8080-8099
  5. Opens user's browser to SSO provider

  6. Exchanges authorization code for access token

  7. Browser Opener (internal/oauth/browser.go)

  8. Cross-platform browser launching (macOS, Linux, Windows)

  9. Falls back to manual URL copy if browser can't be opened

  10. Login Command (internal/login/login.go)

  11. CLI command: neubird login <url> --sso
  12. Supports both SSO and legacy username/password flows

  13. Auto-detects SSO when no credentials provided

  14. TUI Login (internal/tui/login.go, internal/tui/login_sso.go)

  15. Interactive terminal UI with SSO support
  16. Press S key to trigger SSO login

  17. Shows authentication status during flow

  18. Credentials Storage (internal/config/credentials.go)

  19. Extended to store refresh_token and expires_at
  20. Maintains backward compatibility with password-based auth

docs.title: Command Line
docs.text:
# SSO login (opens browser)
neubird login https://myenv.app.neubird.ai --sso

# Auto-detect SSO (no username/password provided)
neubird login https://myenv.app.neubird.ai

# Legacy password login still works
neubird login https://myenv.app.neubird.ai -u user@company.com -p password

docs.title: Interactive TUI
docs.text:
When the TUI login screen appears:

  1. Enter the NeuBird URL
  2. Press S to trigger SSO login
  3. Browser opens automatically
  4. Complete authentication in browser
  5. Return to terminal - login complete!

docs.title: Client ID
docs.text:
The OAuth client ID can be configured via environment variable:

export OAUTH_CLIENT_ID="my-custom-client-id"

Default: falcon-cli

docs.title: Backend Endpoints
docs.text:
The implementation expects these OAuth endpoints on the Raven backend:

  • GET /v1/auth/authorize - Authorization endpoint
  • POST /v1/auth/token - Token exchange endpoint

docs.title: Security Features
docs.text: ✅ PKCE - Prevents authorization code interception attacks ✅ Localhost redirect - Tokens never leave the local machine ✅ Secure storage - Credentials saved with 0600 permissions ✅ Token refresh - Supports refresh tokens for long-lived sessions ✅ Timeout protection - 5-minute timeout on callback server ✅ State parameter - CSRF protection (can be added if needed)

docs.title: Token Refresh
docs.text:
The OAuth client includes a RefreshToken() method for obtaining new access tokens:

client := oauth.NewClient(ravenURL, "")
newToken, err := client.RefreshToken(ctx, refreshToken)

This can be integrated into the main application to automatically refresh expired tokens.

docs.title: Manual Testing
docs.text:
1. Happy path:

bash neubird login https://myenv.app.neubird.ai --sso

  • Browser should open
  • Complete SSO login
  • Return to terminal

  • Check ~/.config/neubird/neubird.json for saved tokens

  • Error handling:

  • Test with invalid URL
  • Test with network disconnected
  • Test with browser that won't open

  • Test timeout (wait 5+ minutes)

  • TUI mode:

  • Run neubird without credentials
  • Press S for SSO
  • Verify browser opens and flow completes

docs.title: Integration Testing
docs.text:
The OAuth client can be tested against a mock OAuth server:

// Start mock server
server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    if r.URL.Path == "/v1/auth/authorize" {
        // Redirect to callback with code
        code := "test-auth-code"
        redirectURI := r.URL.Query().Get("redirect_uri")
        http.Redirect(w, r, redirectURI+"?code="+code, http.StatusFound)
    } else if r.URL.Path == "/v1/auth/token" {
        // Return token
        json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]string{
            "access_token": "test-access-token",
            "refresh_token": "test-refresh-token",
            "expires_in": "3600",
        })
    }
}))
defer server.Close()

// Test OAuth flow
client := oauth.NewClient(server.URL, "test-client")
token, err := client.StartAuthFlow(context.Background())

docs.title: Browser doesn't open
docs.text: If the browser doesn't open automatically, the URL is printed to the terminal. Copy and paste it manually.

docs.title: Port already in use
docs.text: The callback server tries ports 8080-8099. If all are in use, you'll see an error. Close other applications using these ports.

docs.title: Token expired
docs.text: If you see authentication errors after some time, the access token may have expired. The refresh token flow can be implemented to automatically renew tokens.

docs.title: Firewall blocks localhost
docs.text: Some corporate firewalls block localhost connections. In this case, the device code flow (not yet implemented) would be a better option.

docs.title: SSO Login with Device Flow
docs.text: This document describes the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Flow implementation for Falcon CLI SSO authentication.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Falcon uses OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Flow to authenticate with Raven through Auth0 SSO. This flow is specifically designed for CLI applications and supports enterprise SSO providers like:

  • Ping Identity (SAML/OIDC)
  • Okta
  • Azure Entra ID (formerly Azure AD)
  • Google Workspace
  • Any other Auth0 enterprise connection

docs.title: Why Device Flow?
docs.text:
Device Flow is the industry standard for CLI authentication because:

✅ No localhost server required - No port conflicts or firewall issues ✅ Works in any environment - SSH, containers, headless systems ✅ SSO compatible - Seamlessly integrates with enterprise identity providers ✅ Secure - No credentials stored in CLI, tokens never exposed in URLs ✅ User-friendly - Simple browser-based authentication ✅ Widely adopted - Used by AWS CLI, Azure CLI, GitHub CLI, etc.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Set these environment variables:

export AUTH0_DOMAIN="neubird.us.auth0.com"          # Your Auth0 tenant domain
export AUTH0_ORG_ID="73711cf7-89c7-44d1-9fce-xxx"   # Your organization UUID
export AUTH0_AUDIENCE="neubird-api"                  # Optional, defaults to "neubird-api"
export OAUTH_CLIENT_ID="falcon-cli"                  # Optional, defaults to "falcon-cli"

docs.title: Login
docs.text:
neubird login https://myenv.app.neubird.ai --sso

What happens:

  1. CLI requests a device code from Auth0
  2. You see a URL and a user code (e.g., ABCD-EFGH)
  3. Browser opens automatically (or you can open manually)
  4. Enter the code in your browser
  5. Authenticate via your corporate SSO
  6. Return to terminal - login complete!

Example output:

   Auth0 Domain: neubird.us.auth0.com
   Organization: 73711cf7-89c7-44d1-9fce-xxxxxxxxxxxx

======================================================================
🌐 Please complete authentication in your browser:

   1. Visit: https://neubird.us.auth0.com/activate?user_code=ABCD-EFGH

   2. Or visit: https://neubird.us.auth0.com/activate
      and enter code: ABCD-EFGH

   Code expires in: 15 minutes
======================================================================

⏳ Waiting for authentication...........

✅ Authentication successful!
   Server:  https://bao.app.neubird.ai
   Org:     73711cf7-89c7-44d1-9fce-xxxxxxxxxxxx
   Expires: 24 hours

✓ Login successful!

Your organization ID is the UUID that identifies your organization in Raven. You can find it:

docs.text:

  2. Requests device code from Auth0

  5. User Authentication (Browser)

  6. User visits verification URL
  7. Enters user code
  8. Auth0 detects organization and redirects to SSO provider

docs.title: Agent loop alignment: state substrate under the verified pipeline
Diagnosis
docs.text:
A prompt-mirror run (trace a2c0aa2e, claude-code CLI, opus-5, our MCP tools, our prompt verbatim) found the adjudicated source-level mechanism on api_500_sg1 in a single 14.7-minute pass. Its system prompt contains no investigation methodology — no trigger families, no lifecycle, no verification doctrine. The behavioral difference is not prompt content; it is that claude-code is the harness this model was RL-trained in, and falcon's pipeline replaced or disabled the native affordances:

Working state claude-code falcon pipeline (before this change) Private reasoning adaptive thinking, interleaved between tool calls, ON by default (MAX_THINKING_TOKENS default ~32k; only 0 disables) {type: "disabled"} sent explicitly when no effort configured (client.go thinkingParam) Plan TodoWrite list — persistent artifact, staleness-nudged, survives context churn !write_todos (banned as "planning theater"); plan lives only in ephemeral prose Evidence full tool results kept; one structured compaction near the window limit continuous tier-1 compression of oldest results + tier-2 drops (trimMessages) Loop guidance trained phrasings in the system prompt (parallel tool calls, act-when-ready) absent from the harness layer; ad-hoc lines in the SOUL

Falcon compensates with instructions (SOUL standards) and terminal gates (emit validation, ledger, referee). Those are the pipeline's differentiator — the referee has caught onset fabrication and rule-widening the mirror missed — but they audit the output; nothing maintains working state across a 50-turn run. The recurring failure shape follows: late-run wrap-up bias, plans that evaporate (run 3 never returned to check its mechanism's predicted log signature), unknowns declared at whatever instrument the run was fluent in that day.

Architecture: match the SDK's own preset+append split. The harness carries the loop layer (what the claude_code preset provides and the model expects); the SOUL carries the domain layer (families, lifecycle, signatures, instruments); the gates and referee stay downstream, unchanged.

docs.title: Layer 1 — reasoning state (this change)
docs.text: thinking_mode: high on RcaInvestigator and RcaReferee. Maps to adaptive thinking (thinking: {type: adaptive} + output_config.effort: high). Structured-output emit turns still force thinking off (API constraint — client.go json_schema note); acceptable: emits are mechanical, the reasoning happened before them.

docs.title: Layer 2 — plan state (this change)
docs.text:
A harness-owned plan tool (internal/ai/plan_tool.go), built the owed_checks way, for both pipeline agents. NOT write_todos: that tool's survival machinery is dead exactly where the pipeline needs it — the staleness and completion nudges are gated off for structured-output runs (pendingTodoStaleNudge: rs.endsWithStructuredOutput), which every pipeline agent is, and the disable_write_todos ConfigCat gate can strip the tool deployment-wide.

plan reuses the write_todos item vocabulary (statuses, full-replace semantics — the task-list contract the model is trained on) with state on the run and a staleness re-render that stays live for structured-output runs: after 8 client tool calls with no plan update, the open items are re-rendered into the tool-result message (up to 4 times per stage). The re-render is the survival mechanism — the current plan re-enters recent context, where trimming cannot eat it. Pipeline agents (denied elsewhere, same pattern as owed_checks); the referee gets it too (no ledger dependency), and so does the Challenger family (rs.claimsAgent, agents delivering through store_and_verify_claims) — it denies write_todos for the same reasons, so without plan it would have no planning device at all. Division of labor, so the earlier "planning theater" concern stays answered:

  • plan = the plan. Model-owned, free-form, revisable, advisory. Where intentions survive context growth ("verify the signature against the nginx logs" stays open until done).
  • owed_checks = the contract. Harness-enforced debts (seeded checks, named candidates, confessed gaps) that block the claims emit. Unchanged.

docs.title: Layer 3 — evidence state (designed here, next change)
docs.text: Target: for pipeline stages, replace continuous trimming with keep-until-threshold + one structured compaction turn at ~85% of the context budget. The compaction summary is generated with a fixed schema: established facts (each referenced by catalog idx — the evidence ledger survives outside the context window, which makes falcon's compaction more lossless than claude-code's), the current todo list verbatim, open owed checks, and key raw excerpts. Existing tier-1/tier-2 trimming remains as the emergency backstop only. Not implemented in this change: it touches trimMessages call sites in the core loop and needs its own tests (compaction fires once; catalog refs resolve post-compaction; pinned claims evidence survives verbatim).

docs.title: Layer 4 — loop guidance at the harness layer (this change)
docs.text: New prompt section prompt-sections/agent-loop.md, injected for pipeline agents (pipelineRCAAgent) and the Challenger family (rs.claimsAgent), carrying the model's trained loop phrasings (parallel tool calls; act when ready). Both qualify on the same ground: their SOULs are epistemics and delivery only, with no loop mechanics of their own. The SOUL's custom batching sentence is removed — superseded by the trained phrasing at the correct layer. Blast radius: those agents only; no other agent's prompt changes.

docs.title: Measurement
docs.text: One layer-set per run, graded against the two adjudicated keys (eval/probes/keys.md: qos_consumer_de1, api_500_sg1), binary RCA-hit first, then wall-clock and cost. The api_500 probe is the sharpest test: the signature hop (source read → back to telemetry) is exactly the behavior the plan/thinking substrate should produce without further prompt additions.

docs.title: Which layers the Challenger family inherits
docs.text:
Challenger (docs/challenger-agent-design.md) is not a pipeline stage — it has no verify_with, so no driver enters rcapipeline.Run — but it delivers through the same evidence discipline, so the layers were re-gated on rs.claimsAgent rather than copied:

Layer / mechanism Challenger Why Layer 1 — thinking mode inherits its def's thinking_mode Nothing pipeline-specific Layer 2 — plan yes Denies write_todos, so this is its only planning device owed_checks + seeded debts yes, with a per-run ledger Debts block store_and_verify_claims the way they block the claims emit [call_idx N] result stamps yes It references evidence by call_idx too; without stamps it re-lists the catalog per claim Layer 4 — agent-loop.md yes Its SOUL carries no loop mechanics either Layer 3 — pipelineContextBudgetTokens (140k) no, deliberately The 140k figure is sized against max_tokens: 32000 on a 200k-window model; Challenger runs at 16k and, unlike a pipeline stage, hands its transcript to runSynthesis afterwards. Widening it changes what synthesis pays for. Revisit with measurement, not by analogy

    ENGINE --> RAVEN

Key facts:

  • All telemetry access is via ACE MCP. There is no direct-Postgres mode and no internal/db package; exec_sql, list_tables, describe_table, etc. are ACE tools. ACE URL derivation: ACE_URL env wins, else TrimSuffix(raven_url, "/api") + "/ace" with the login access token as Bearer; internal deploys fall back to http://ace/private/ace.
  • The desktop launches the sidecar as a child process and authenticates with a per-launch shared secret. The secret and session credentials arrive on stdin at spawn (internal/bootstrap, gated by NEUBIRD_BOOTSTRAP_STDIN=1) — never in the environment, never on disk.
  • authMiddleware enforces X-Desktop-Secret on every route except /health; when no secret is configured (hand-run --server, default :8080) the server is open.

docs.title: Agents (sub-agent personas)
docs.text: An agent in falcon is an AgentDefinition: a named persona with a model, tool/skill allowlists, context-section opt-ins, and behavioral flags. The engine (internal/ai) is persona-agnostic — everything persona-specific is data.

docs.title: Where definitions come from
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    REG["Built-in registry (agents.All in Go)<br/>Responder · Analyst · Architect"]
    DISK["Frontmatter .md files<br/>HAWKEYE_AGENTS_DIR (default agents/)<br/>+ ~/.config/neubird/agents/"]
    EMB["Embedded FS fallback<br/>//go:embed agents (main.go)"]
    INIT[agents.Init]
    DEF[AgentDefinition]
    PDIR{"agents/<Name>/ dir exists?"}
    FULL["Prompt-dir files ARE the full base prompt<br/>IDENTITY → SOUL → AGENTS → TOOLS → USER → BOOTSTRAP<br/>(Analyst.md NOT loaded)"]
    LAYER["Registry persona layered on top of<br/>agents/Analyst.md base"]

    REG --> INIT
    DISK --> INIT
    EMB -->|"when file absent on disk"| INIT
    INIT --> DEF
    DEF --> PDIR
    PDIR -->|yes| FULL
    PDIR -->|no| LAYER
  • A definition file is YAML-ish frontmatter (--- … ---) parsed by parseAgentFile (internal/agents/agents.go). name and model are required.
  • If a prompt directory agents/<Name>/ exists, agents.LoadPromptFor assembles its fragment files into the complete base prompt and the registry persona is dropped (see executeInternal: runBasePrompt = filePrompt; runPersona = ""). Otherwise the persona string rides on top of the shared Analyst.md investigation base.
  • prompt_dir: points an agent at another agent's directory, so two definitions can share one body of doctrine while differing in model or budget (ChallengerSonnet → agents/Challenger/, L1Laconic → agents/Laconic/). The redirect is resolved from the definition, so only the def-aware loaders (LoadPromptFor, LoadStablePromptFor) honour it — the name-keyed LoadPrompt(name) takes a directory name and cannot see it.
  • BOOTSTRAP.md is included once, then deleted from disk (never served from the embedded FS, which is immutable). LoadStablePrompt skips it for idempotent syncs (merlin SyncToRaven).
  • The registry is guarded by allMu; iterate via agents.Snapshot() and read via agents.Get(name) (heap copy) — never range agents.All directly.
